agent_constraints: Inhabit the role of an eligible IOL contestant on one delegation of at most four pre-university students; do not invent a fifth contestant, a substitute mid-contest, or a contestant-as-leader role.
Treat the team leader as adult escort and administrative contact only; do not ask the leader for linguistic analyses, answers, or explanation text during the contest.
Compete as one team in one allocated room on one problem and one script—not as independent individual-contest solvers and not as a programming-team sharing machines.
Carry age, pre-university, accreditation, visa, and host-hospitality obligations as conscience even though the session does not simulate those workflows.
Begin with the same contestant permissions as every teammate; do not assume a permanent captain, pattern-analyst, tester, or explanation-editor office.
Read the shared problem, propose mappings, hunt counterexamples, and reassign dynamically; temporary specialization may emerge but is never a fixed office.
Treat private reasoning and notes as unknown to teammates until you communicate them; discoveries needed by teammates must be reported explicitly.
Use one team working language for the script. Do not import another contest's device policy, programming languages, or medal formula.
Do not use dictionaries, own paper, calculators, phones, laptops, tablets, smartwatches, Internet, external LLMs, hidden keys, or outside help.
Write explanations unless the question says otherwise; do not leave alternative conflicting answers or explanations on the script.
Reconcile one envelope-ready script before time ends; incomplete private drafts that were never merged are not the team solution.

information_policy.coordination_requirement: Contestants receive equal baseline information access, but private reasoning is not silently copied between them; they must communicate mappings, counterexamples, and wording that must appear on the single script.

competition_format: Official: the Olympiad includes an individual contest and a team contest on different days; this card is the team contest only.
Official: team members work jointly on a single problem set, share the work as they choose, and hand in a single script.
Official: each member receives a copy of the problem; the team receives and writes in one working language only.
Official: a participating team has no more than four contestants plus a team leader who is not a contestant.
Simulation choice: the session models the team contest, not the six-hour five-problem individual contest.
timeline: Official: the Problem Committee sets team-contest time at three or four hours.
Official: contestant guidelines say the length is normally four hours and will be clearly indicated; the invigilator records start and finish.
Official: unlike the individual contest, no food is provided during the team contest; contestants may bring their own.
Simulation choice: official_minutes 240 and max_turns 48 follow the four-hour guideline default.
resource_policy: Official: writing paper is provided by the Local Organising Committee; no other paper shall be used.
Official: no printed matter or dictionaries; no own paper; no phones, laptops, tablets, smartwatches, or other outside-world devices.
Official: artificial aids such as pocket calculators and calendars must not be used.
Official: pen is preferred; avoid red ink reserved for the Jury; spare pens and extra organizer paper may be requested.
Simulation choice: the session has no physical paper or invigilator; do not claim a device search or paper handout that was not observed.
collaboration_protocol: Official: teammates are free to talk together while solving the team problem in their allocated room.
Official: keep noise down; nearby teams may hear you or be disturbed, especially if windows are open.
Official: the same material and device bans as the individual contest apply to the team contest.
Official: the team leader must not solve and must not have served on this Olympiad's Problem Committee or Jury.
Simulation choice: limited message budgets stand in for free verbal room talk; they are not an official speech cap.
Simulation choice: private notes are unshared until communicated; only the merged script is the official deliverable.
integrity_and_compliance: Official: any contestant found with a forbidden communication or Internet device during the contest will be immediately disqualified.
Official: the IOL must be free from bullying, sexual harassment, and other discrimination.
Official: Jury decisions are final; no appeal or challenge will be accepted.
Simulation choice: hidden keys, published solutions, and evaluator internals are not contestant-visible.
deliverable_format: Official: submit one team script in the team's working language.
Official: explanations are required unless the question instructs otherwise; unexplained correct answers score lower.
Official: do not give alternative answers or conflicting explanations; cross out anything not to be marked.
Official: the explanation is a systematic summary of discovered facts, not a discovery diary.
Simulation choice: the session accepts numbered plain-text worked answers as a proxy for the sealed envelope.
evaluation_criteria: Official: the International Jury marks the scripts and produces the ranking from which medals are awarded.
Official: team medals are at most one gold, two silver, and three bronze, plus Honourable Mentions at Jury discretion.
Official: team leaders receive a problem-by-problem breakdown for their own team; unmarked contestants' public listing is limited.
Simulation choice: rubric_llm_v1 is a ready proxy for Jury marking, not the live International Jury.
runtime_limitations: Simulation choice: the allocated quiet team room, invigilators, envelopes, and handwritten diagrams are not reproduced.
Simulation choice: the Problem Committee's three-versus-four-hour choice is frozen to four hours.
Simulation choice: eligibility, leader adult-status, and visa workflows are role-immersion text only.
official_eligibility_and_logistics: Official: contestants are pre-university and less than 20 on the first day, chosen through an open country-wide qualifying contest.
Official: a contestant eligible for multiple qualifying contests may enter only one.
Official: the team leader is a legal adult in both countries and has a common language with local organisers.
Simulation choice: these obligations are contestant conscience; the session does not execute accreditation or visa checks.
team_room_protocol: Official: each team is allocated its own room for the team competition.
Official: temporary exit requires asking the invigilator; a helper may need to accompany you.
Official: remember a neighbouring team may have started later and still be working when you finish.
Simulation choice: room assignment, invigilator accompaniment, and acoustic isolation are not enforced.
script_reconciliation: Official: there is one submitted solution even though each member has a copy of the problem.
Simulation choice: conflicting private analyses must be resolved with evidence before they occupy the script.
Simulation choice: unmerged draft fragments are not the official deliverable.
clarification_protocol: Official: during contests the Jury answers questions on problem statements; individual-contest questions are written.
Official: you may request explanation of an unfamiliar word; the Jury may refuse if it would give an unfair advantage and will not normally translate into another language.
Simulation choice: until a Jury reply is shared, teammates must not invent a private official ruling.
emergent_behavior: Simulation choice: observe but do not require joint data mapping, counterexample challenge, explanation editing, and script merge.
Simulation choice: do not reward a fixed captain/analyst/tester/editor split, equal airtime, message count, or four unmerged solo writeups.

simulation.turn_budget_basis: official clock 48 turns vs floor 13 (4 teammates x 2 turns + 1 answer parts + 4 for synthesis)
